FROM: STEPHEN LAMB

Dear Brian & Ron,

Outlet is very good. It is an
excellent idea and I hope it
will continue to thrive. There
are a couple of features which I
think are unnecessary though.
They are Top Ten Games and
Jigblox. I am not sure of the

regular column about the
Spectrum which is called "On

FROM: FRANK HARROP

Dear Ron and Brian,

Many thanks for Outlet issue 5,
and I'm quite impressed with the
opening titles and musical
accompaniment! You mentioned
cartridge storage- well I
solved it cheaply and easily by
using the boxes in which 35mm.
slides are returned from
processing when plastic mounted.

Each half section holds 6
cartridges neatly upright - a
total of 12 to a box, and if you
are lucky to get the boxes with
clear lids you can see all the
cartridge details through it.

There seems to be a small bug in
the calendar programme in Outlet
4 - try entering 1935, 1989 or
1995 (there may be others) and
you get the report "3. Subscript
wrong 730:1" perhaps Norman
Unitt can say why?

Finally, although "Microdrive
doctor" is no longer available,
if you find an unreliable sector
when formatting, then the RAMDOS
programme from ROYBOT will
enable you to 'busy' that sector
under the 'Recovery' section,
and it will not be usable.

By the way, with Tasword Three
you can re-format down to 32
from 64 characters a line just
by using Ext.H!

Keep up the good work both of
you,
        Sincerely, FRANK HARROP.


Thanks for storage tip, Frank.It
complements other suggestions in
this issue.That RAMDOS looks OK.
We'll try to get a copy to check
it out. Funny bug in Calendar...
To think I tested every year
EXCEPT 1935, 1989 and 1995!
(Ahem!)          - Brian

FROM:JOHN McCLEAVE, POOLE,DORSET

Dear Brian & Ron,

    Nice to have met you both at
the Show. Glad to hear that
everything is taking-off with
'Outlet', and I'm sure that
membership will swell especially
after the show introductions.

    Have you heard anymore
concerning the 'Swift Disc'
Microdrive Emulator? That could
be interesting. I have manually
converted 'Outlet 1' to Swift-
Disc apart from one small
intriguing point. For some
reason 'Jotter' will not load
from the Menu. The program name
'Jotter' is not accepted, giving

a FILE NOT FOUND Report. I have
tried various ways to overcome
the problem, but unsuccessfully.
Try it! My hopes were to put
maybe six or seven 'Outlets'
onto one disc, but I can foresee
problems as many programs run
under the same name in every
issue.  Any ideas?

    Hope you can manage to keep
        up the good work,
          all the best,

          John McCleave


TO: JOHN McCLEAVE FROM BRIAN

Compare the spelling of JOTTER
in line 30 of CONTENTS with the
saved name. Are they both in
capital letters? Does JOTTER
load manually - apart from the
CONTENTS?

To get multiple OUTLETs on one
disc alter common names by
adding a suffix: 1, 2 etc.
(shorten name if more than 10
characters) then alter line 30
in the relevant CONTENTS. BUT IF
A FILE HAS THE TOKEN "CODE" AT
THE END IT MUST REMAIN THE 10TH
CHARACTER! So for example:
"letters  CODE" could be:
"letters1 CODE" but NOT:
"letters CODE1" !

Likewise, alter each CONTENTS to
CONTENTS1, CONTENTS2 etc. Then
EVERY program would need to be
altered at the line that returns
to CONTENTS and often NEXT ITEM!
To find the relevant lines in
each program put a blank disc in
your drive and select "RETURN TO
CONTENTS" in each program and
note the line number in the
"File not found" message! Even
then, without testing it, I
can't guarantee there won't be
other problems!

No, we've had no chance to look
at the emulator. It will be some
time before we get to the Swift
Disc version of OUTLET!
                        - Brian

I've just checked Tasword 2 with
my Alphacom and it works OK.
That is, using extended mode "P"
WITHIN THE TEXT EDITOR, not from
the menu. Try this: use STOP
(symbol + "A") and select "b" to
enter BASIC. EDIT line 20 and
put COPY : just before the CLS
command. Re-enter the line and
run the program. Now type in

some text and then use STOP
again.You should find the screen
copied to your printer. If this
fails check that your printer is
working normally by entering
BASIC and just LPRINT something.
Is the printer switched on?! If
the COPY worked, however, then
your TASWORD may be faulty. Let
me know if you have no luck at
all as I can write you a small
BASIC patch that will do the
job.

TIMEX paper is available from
MICROSNIPS AT `9.95(see OUTBOARD
for address)

TO: STEVE MONK FROM BRIAN

Thanks Steve. One of the best
reviews I've seen was for the
Amstrad DMP 2000 but I'd already
bought my BROTHER M1009. I think
the M1109 you mentioned is a
later, superior version. I used
to avidly read all the printer
reviews but there are so many
printers available now I'm out
of touch!

Using Interface 1 is reasonable
but you will miss not being able
to use COPY at the touch of a
key. (You can still buy software
to do a COPY of course).The main
advantage with I/F 1 is that you
already have it! Of course, if
you choose a printer with only a
centronics interface you won't

be able to use it thru' I/F 1
and will have to get another
printer interface.

If you decide to use the +2s own
RS232 port then to send control
codes (margin settings etc.-see
the manual of the printer you
get) you will need POKE 23349,39
and POKE 23350,1 first. Use
POKE 23349,36 and POKE 23350,1
afterwards. (I don't think this
is mentioned in the +2 manual).
Incidentally, I hope to produce
an alphabetical keyword look-up
table for printer control codes
in a future issue of OUTLET as
my printer manual is useless for
quick reference.

The other problem is getting a

cable. Microsnips (see OUTBOARD
for address) sell I/F 1 leads at
`9.95. They also advertise the
following printers:

SEIKOSHA SP-180......`149.95
PANASONIC KX-P1081...`179.95
AMSTRAD DMP 2160.....`159.95

It may be worth writing to them
for info on what each printer
has to offer.

Tasman Software of Springfield
House, Hyde Terrace, Leeds LS2
9LN (Tel: 0532 438301)sell I/F1
cables and +2 RS232 cables at
`14.50. They also sell their own
centronics printer interface
with cable at `29.90 but you
need to load software to use it

which you may find a pain. I'd
prefer the Kempston E which, I
think,needs no extra software to
run it. It's available from
Microsnips at `39.95.

At the same price is MULTIPRINT
from Romantic Robot (address in
OUTBOARD) or `34.95 without a
through-port! It's a centronics
interface which has numerous
features including COPY and can
dump from WITHIN ANY PROGRAM at
the touch of a button! This may
be the one to go for. It seems
to be supplied with a cable.

Our readers have a wide range of
printers and interfaces so,
unless you are in a desperate
hurry,wait a month or two to see
what first-hand info comes in.

Sorry I don't have recent info
on printers themselves but may I
ask our readers to write if they
can recommend a particular one?
Make sure it's Epson-compatible
whichever one you get. As for
WHERE you will buy it - you will
clearly have to use mail-order
if your local shops cannot help.
I would urge you to buy PERSONAL
COMPUTER WORLD which has a wide
range of printer adverts. You
should find them all there and
can choose the best price (check
if VAT is included)I'll look out
for further info myself.
                   - Brian

FROM: ADRIAN STOCKS

Dear Ron & Brian,
Many thanks for OUTLET 5 which
arrived this morning. I've had a
quick whizz through it and it's
well up to your usual standard:
BUT!-Please do not even consider
publishing Andy Pennell's stream
14 to Z$ routine without his
permission, especially after he
has specifically requested
otherwise. This would be just
the sort of action that would
bring a worthwhile enterprise
into disrepute. If it was a
computer program we should
condemn it as piracy. You have
the book and therefore know the
publisher - they would give you
Andy's address or forward a
letter for you.

I note that E.M. Duffield
mentions in a letter (OUTLET 5)
that he uses a Brother EP44; I
would be very interested to see
what he has done with it. If you
are not already aware, it is an
LCD display electronic type-
writer which also has a built-in
RS232 interface so that it can
not only be used as a computer
printer but can also memorise an
A4 page of text and cough it up
on request into a computer. I
have used mine very successfully
with the Rotronics Wafadrive and
would indeed have got it linked
up to the Interface I had not
Messrs W.H. Smith and Messrs.
Brother between them shomehow
managed to lose it since I took
it in to Smith's for repair IN

AUGUST! They are trying to sort
out whose fault it is.

My point in mentioning the EP44
is that it is very handy to sit
quietly typing a letter or what-
ever and then when convenient
converting what it holds into a
Tasword II or Spectral Writer
textfile. I have written a Basic
program to do just this for the
Wafadrive and it should convert
happily for the Microdrive but
it obviously relies on inputting
to the Interface I RS232 port
and I might have the problem
that E.M. Duffield has apparent-
ly solved.When/if I ever get the
EP44 back I'll send the program
to you for possible inclusion.

 Yours sincerely, Adrian Stocks

FROM: MICK FLOREY,  Felixstowe

I MAY have the information you
are looking for regarding the +3
(and I might not).

I have the Opus disk with 128K
(Sinclair). The Opus would not
work at first so a different
EPROM had to be fitted. The
information supplied with the
Opus said that the RAM disk
(which uses the extra memory) is
not NORMALLY useable in 48K mode
but instead of going in 48K mode
via menu, use the following
method: Enter 128K BASIC (YUK)
and, if you know how, enter as a
direct command: PRINT USR 0.
press ENTER and presto! - you're
in 48K mode WITHOUT disabling
the Paging system and can still

use the RAM disk. Note that the
Opus EPROM actually extends the
BASIC and adds some extra
commands including the ability
to FORMAT 6; " RAM DISK". If now
a CAT 6 is done, a CAT is done
of the RAMDISK.

There is a method [available]
for getting back into 128K mode
via a 6-10 byte machine code
program...

Hope this info is useful. I was
going to send it a while ago but
assumed somebody else would send
it!

OUTLET is getting better! -
"That's The Ticket!" in No.5 was
really good!       - MICK FLOREY

#### TO: JOHN McCLEAVE FROM BRIAN

Compare the spelling of JOTTER in line 30 of CONTENTS with the saved name. Are they both in capital letters? Does JOTTER load manually - apart from the CONTENTS?

To get multiple OUTLETs on one disc alter common names by adding a suffix: 1, 2 etc. (shorten name if more than 10 characters) then alter line 30 in the relevant CONTENTS. BUT IF A FILE HAS THE TOKEN "CODE" AT THE END IT MUST REMAIN THE 10TH CHARACTER! So for example:  
`"letters  CODE"` could be:  
`"letters1 CODE"` but NOT:  
`"letters CODE1"`!

Likewise, alter each CONTENTS to CONTENTS1, CONTENTS2 etc. Then EVERY program would need to be altered at the line that returns to CONTENTS and often NEXT ITEM! To find the relevant lines in each program put a blank disc in your drive and select "RETURN TO CONTENTS" in each program and note the line number in the "File not found" message! Even then, without testing it, I can't guarantee there won't be other problems!

No, we've had no chance to look at the emulator. It will be some time before we get to the Swift Disc version of OUTLET!

— Brian

### TO: STEVE MONK FROM BRIAN

Thanks Steve. One of the best reviews I've seen was for the Amstrad DMP 2000 but I'd already bought my BROTHER M1009. I think the M1109 you mentioned is a later, superior version. I used to avidly read all the printer reviews but there are so many printers available now I'm out of touch!

Using Interface 1 is reasonable but you will miss not being able to use COPY at the touch of a key. (You can still buy software to do a COPY of course). The main advantage with I/F 1 is that you already have it! Of course, if you choose a printer with only a centronics interface you won't be able to use it thru' I/F 1 and will have to get another printer interface.

If you decide to use the +2s own RS232 port then to send control codes (margin settings etc.-see the manual of the printer you get) you will need `POKE 23349,39` and `POKE 23350,1` first. Use `POKE 23349,36` and `POKE 23350,1` afterwards. (I don't think this is mentioned in the +2 manual). Incidentally, I hope to produce an alphabetical keyword look-up table for printer control codes in a future issue of OUTLET as my printer manual is useless for quick reference.

The other problem is getting a cable. Microsnips (see OUTBOARD for address) sell I/F 1 leads at £9.95. They also advertise the following printers:

| Printer | Price |
|---|---|
| SEIKOSHA SP-180 | £149.95 |
| PANASONIC KX-P1081 | £179.95 |
| AMSTRAD DMP 2160 | £159.95 |

It may be worth writing to them for info on what each printer has to offer.

Tasman Software of Springfield House, Hyde Terrace, Leeds LS2 9LN (Tel: 0532 438301) sell I/F1 cables and +2 RS232 cables at £14.50. They also sell their own centronics printer interface with cable at £29.90 but you need to load software to use it which you may find a pain. I'd prefer the Kempston E which, I think, needs no extra software to run it. It's available from Microsnips at £39.95.

At the same price is MULTIPRINT from Romantic Robot (address in OUTBOARD) or £34.95 without a through-port! It's a centronics interface which has numerous features including COPY and can dump from WITHIN ANY PROGRAM at the touch of a button! This may be the one to go for. It seems to be supplied with a cable.

Our readers have a wide range of printers and interfaces so, unless you are in a desperate hurry, wait a month or two to see what first-hand info comes in.

Sorry I don't have recent info on printers themselves but may I ask our readers to write if they can recommend a particular one? Make sure it's Epson-compatible whichever one you get. As for WHERE you will buy it - you will clearly have to use mail-order if your local shops cannot help. I would urge you to buy PERSONAL COMPUTER WORLD which has a wide range of printer adverts. You should find them all there and can choose the best price (check if VAT is included) I'll look out for further info myself.

Если теперь набрать `CAT 6`, отобразится каталог RAM-диска.

Есть способ [доступный] вернуться обратно в режим 128K с помощью программки в машинных кодах длиной 6-10 байт...
